Sure! Below is a quick reference you can copy‑paste into a terminal (or your favorite HTTP client) to pull up to 10 files that have communicated with the IP **12.234.56.126** on VirusTotal.  

> **⚠️** Replace `my_api` with your *real* VirusTotal API key before running the command.

```bash
curl -X GET "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/files?limit=10&cursor=pointer" \
     -H "x-apikey: my_api"
```

### What this does

| Parameter | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `limit=10` | Returns at most 10 file objects per request. |
| `cursor=pointer` | If you’re paginating, set this to the cursor value returned from the previous call. (If this is your first request, you can omit it.) |
| `x-apikey` | Your API key – required for authentication. |

### Response format

The API will return a JSON payload that looks roughly like this:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "file_id_1",
      "type": "file",
      "attributes": {
        "last_analysis_stats": { ... },
        "last_analysis_results": { ... },
        "magic": "PE32 executable",
        "size": 123456,
        "sha256": "..."
      }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "links": {
    "next": "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/files?limit=10&cursor=next_cursor_value"
  },
  "meta": {
    "cursor": "next_cursor_value"
  }
}
```

- **`data`** – array of file objects that have communicated with the IP.  
- **`links.next`** – URL to fetch the next page (if any).  
- **`meta.cursor`** – the cursor value you’ll use for the next request.

### Using the cursor

If you want to fetch the next batch of files, simply replace `pointer` in the URL with the cursor value returned in `meta.cursor`:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/12.234.56.126/files?limit=10&cursor=next_cursor_value" \
     -H "x-apikey: my_api"
```

### Quick Python snippet

If you prefer Python, here’s a minimal example using `requests`:

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "my_api"
IP = "12.234.56.126"
LIMIT = 10
CURSOR = "pointer"   # or None for the first page

url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{IP}/files"
params = {"limit": LIMIT}
if CURSOR != "pointer":
    params["cursor"] = CURSOR

headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY}

resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
print(resp.json())
```

Feel free to tweak the `LIMIT` or add additional query parameters (e.g., `sort`, `filter`) as needed. Happy hunting!
